newsitem.title: USA: NYS senate defeats casino bill by 41 to 19 margin.
newsitem.headline: NYS senate defeats casino bill by 41 to 19 margin.

text.p: The New York State Senate on Tuesday defeated a bill that would have allowed casino gambling by a margin of 41 to 19, said a reporter in Albany who witnessed the voting.

The Senate Majority Leader, Joseph Bruno, R-Troy, had said he did not know if there enough votes in favor of the measure, which was expected to need the support of Democrat lawmakers if it won approval.

Talk that the Senate Democrats, who are in the minority, had been advised to reject the bill could not be immediately confirmed. There had been speculation that the Democrats might seek to use their leverage over the casino bill to pressure Bruno to soften his stand on other issues, like eliminating rent control, which mainly affects New York City.
Those rules are a key concern for Bruno's counterpart in the Assembly, Speaker Sheldon Silver, D-Manhattan.

Gov. George Pataki, a Republican, had supported the casino measure, saying the state was losing billions of dollars of revenues to out-of-state casinos and ones run by Indians inside the state. The bill would have allowed one casino to be built in Niagara Falls, Buffalo and either Warren or Saratoga Counties, as well as an unlimited number in the Catskills, whose resorts are losing ground to other regions, including casinos in Atlantic City, N.J., and Connecticut.

A previous legislature had approved the bill, but it had to be enacted twice, and would also have had to win the approval of the voters in a referendum. The bill cannot now be called up again in the Senate during this legislative session, a state source explained. The source declined to be named.
